svg.title: $850,000 gross settlements to $199,750 owner profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-owner-profit-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $850,000 gross settlements to $199,750 owner profit; subtitle: Six bars reconcile the 55% retained share and 23.5% gross-basis net margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: The first and last bars are absolute totals; the four intermediate bars are signed deductions. Only the $382,500 acquisition deduction is fixed by the canonical 55% retained share; the remaining $267,750 is allocated illustratively. This model treats the quoted $2,500–$14,000 monthly opex band as recurring pod and platform overhead, with variable fulfillment separately funded. All-in post-acquisition costs average $22,312.50 monthly. If the quoted opex band were intended to include every such cost, it would not reconcile to the canonical Base Case.; caption: $850,000 − $382,500 − $99,750 − $108,000 − $60,000 = $199,750. Retained revenue is $467,500; owner profit is 23.5% of gross settlements and 42.73% of retained revenue. The 55% presentation is the supplied ASC 606 modeling convention; actual principal-versus-agent presentation depends on contract facts.; stages: label: Gross billable settlements; value: $850,000 annual exchange settlement total; numeric value: 850000.0; detail: Opening absolute total equals 3,400 settled calls at $250 each. Keep this gross settlement basis separate from the $467,500 retained-revenue presentation and from any downstream buyer transaction value.; label: Publisher and media acquisition; value: Subtract $382,500; retain $467,500 before other costs; numeric value: -382500.0; detail: Publisher payouts plus click-to-call media consume 45% of gross settlements. Attribute each acquisition cost once; publisher-funded traffic must not also be charged as directly purchased media.; label: Variable call fulfillment; value: Subtract $99,750 in incremental transaction costs; numeric value: -99750.0; detail: Illustrative allocation covers usage-based telephony, metered evidence retrieval, outsourced call audits, and transaction handling. Exclude acquisition spending and fixed subscriptions already represented in other bars.; label: Pod labor and contractors; value: Subtract $108,000 for one employee and two contractors; numeric value: -108000.0; detail: Annual illustrative labor budget equals $9,000 monthly. Treat the full-time seat as paid operating labor; owner profit is the residual after this budget, not a substitute for recording labor expense.; label: Fixed platform and administration; value: Subtract $60,000 in annual recurring overhead; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Budget $5,000 monthly for fixed software commitments, accounting, insurance, and administration. Combined with labor, recurring overhead reaches $14,000 monthly; variable fulfillment remains a separate waterfall deduction.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $199,750 residual after all four modeled deductions; numeric value: 199750.0; detail: Closing absolute total is the canonical Base Case. Conservative remains $200,000 gross, $110,000 retained, and $30,000 profit at 15% gross margin and 27.27% retained margin. Scaled remains $1,500,000 gross, $825,000 retained, and $480,000 profit at 32% and 58.18%, respectively.

rect.title: label: Gross billable settlements; value: $850,000 annual exchange settlement total; numeric value: 850000.0; detail: Opening absolute total equals 3,400 settled calls at $250 each. Keep this gross settlement basis separate from the $467,500 retained-revenue presentation and from any downstream buyer transaction value.

label: Publisher and media acquisition; value: Subtract $382,500; retain $467,500 before other costs; numeric value: -382500.0; detail: Publisher payouts plus click-to-call media consume 45% of gross settlements. Attribute each acquisition cost once; publisher-funded traffic must not also be charged as directly purchased media.

label: Variable call fulfillment; value: Subtract $99,750 in incremental transaction costs; numeric value: -99750.0; detail: Illustrative allocation covers usage-based telephony, metered evidence retrieval, outsourced call audits, and transaction handling. Exclude acquisition spending and fixed subscriptions already represented in other bars.

label: Pod labor and contractors; value: Subtract $108,000 for one employee and two contractors; numeric value: -108000.0; detail: Annual illustrative labor budget equals $9,000 monthly. Treat the full-time seat as paid operating labor; owner profit is the residual after this budget, not a substitute for recording labor expense.

label: Fixed platform and administration; value: Subtract $60,000 in annual recurring overhead; numeric value: -60000.0; detail: Budget $5,000 monthly for fixed software commitments, accounting, insurance, and administration. Combined with labor, recurring overhead reaches $14,000 monthly; variable fulfillment remains a separate waterfall deduction.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $199,750 residual after all four modeled deductions; numeric value: 199750.0; detail: Closing absolute total is the canonical Base Case. Conservative remains $200,000 gross, $110,000 retained, and $30,000 profit at 15% gross margin and 27.27% retained margin. Scaled remains $1,500,000 gross, $825,000 retained, and $480,000 profit at 32% and 58.18%, respectively.
